analysis.purpose: The Java structural parser: turns the token stream into a declaration tree (class, interface, enum, record, method, constructor) plus a flat list of call sites, deliberately stopping short of a full expression parser because the symbol graph only needs declaration spans, nesting, and call-site heads.
responsibilities: Descend the token stream tolerantly, emitting a declaration per construct
Record nesting so members carry qualified names and member-of edges
Collect call sites in a separate whole-stream pass
Degrade on malformed input by skipping the construct rather than throwing
Balance generic angle brackets using the lexer split rule so nested type arguments are skipped correctly

businessRules.rule: Not a full expression parser — a tolerant brace/indent-level descent is enough, and is far less surface area to get wrong.
businessRules.rationale: The symbol graph needs spans, nesting and call heads; parsing expressions would add risk without adding graph value.

businessRules.rule: Field declarations are not emitted as symbols, matching the altitude of the other extractors; their call sites are still captured.
businessRules.rationale: Keeps one consistent notion of what counts as a symbol across languages.

businessRules.rule: Local and anonymous classes inside method bodies are not extracted, because method bodies are consumed rather than descended.
businessRules.rationale: A documented limitation, chosen over a fragile full descent.
